## Architecture And Coding Conventions

- Follow the existing WPF MVVM structure: XAML and code-behind own presentation concerns, view models own UI state and commands, services own persistence and external-process integration, and models remain simple data contracts.
- Use CommunityToolkit.Mvvm attributes and generated commands/properties consistently with nearby code. Avoid adding another MVVM framework or dependency when the existing stack is sufficient.
- Keep nullable reference types enabled and resolve warnings rather than suppressing them without a documented reason.

- Comments should explain non-obvious constraints or rationale. XML documentation belongs on public APIs where inputs, outputs, side effects, or edge cases are not evident.

- Treat ACD overwrite, restore, Git mutation, configuration replacement, downloads, installation, repair, and elevation as safety-sensitive operations.

# AB Logix Git Manager Copilot Instructions

## Operating Workflow

- Treat non-trivial work as a planned workflow. Before editing, identify the concrete behavior, owning code path, smallest viable change, and focused verification that can disprove the approach.
- For work with three or more steps or an architectural decision, maintain a checklist in `tasks/todo.md`. Keep it current as work proceeds and add a short review section with the validation performed and any remaining risks.
- Start from the named file, symbol, failing behavior, test, or command. Read only enough nearby code to form a falsifiable hypothesis, then make the smallest grounded edit.
- After the first substantive edit, immediately run the narrowest available executable check. Repair local failures and rerun that check before widening the scope.
- Use read-only subagents for broad repository exploration, independent review, or parallel research. Give each subagent one focused task and keep implementation ownership in the main agent unless explicitly delegated.
- If evidence invalidates the plan, stop, update the plan, and continue from the newly identified controlling code path.
- Do not declare work complete without verification. Report commands actually run, their result, and anything that could not be validated in the current environment.
- After a user correction, record the generalized lesson in `tasks/lessons.md` so future work does not repeat it.

## Repository Truth And Scope

- Read `README.md` for the current user-facing status and `plan.md` for the canonical product contract, feasibility gates, and acceptance criteria.
- Keep implemented behavior distinct from planned behavior. Verify claims against the current source; never describe a roadmap item as available because it appears in `plan.md`.
- This repository is an early Windows WPF scaffold targeting `net10.0-windows`. Do not assume release packaging, dependency discovery, bundled tools, automated tests, or clean-machine validation exists unless the repository contains evidence.
- Prefer the smallest change that satisfies the request. Do not implement adjacent roadmap items, reformat unrelated code, or overwrite user changes.
- Preserve existing public behavior and configuration compatibility unless the task explicitly requires a breaking change. Call out migrations when changing `%APPDATA%\ABLogixGitManager\config.json` or persisted model shapes.

## Architecture And Coding Conventions

- Follow the existing WPF MVVM structure: XAML and code-behind own presentation concerns, view models own UI state and commands, services own persistence and external-process integration, and models remain simple data contracts.
- Use CommunityToolkit.Mvvm attributes and generated commands/properties consistently with nearby code. Avoid adding another MVVM framework or dependency when the existing stack is sufficient.
- Keep nullable reference types enabled and resolve warnings rather than suppressing them without a documented reason.
- Use clear C# with guard clauses, descriptive names, async APIs for I/O, and cancellation propagation for long-running operations. Keep UI-bound updates on the WPF dispatcher and avoid blocking the UI thread.
- Prefer standard .NET APIs and existing dependencies. Add a package only when it materially simplifies a verified requirement, and document why it is needed.
- Comments should explain non-obvious constraints or rationale. XML documentation belongs on public APIs where inputs, outputs, side effects, or edge cases are not evident.

## Process And Data Safety

- Treat ACD overwrite, restore, Git mutation, configuration replacement, downloads, installation, repair, and elevation as safety-sensitive operations.
- Never claim that an ACD backup exists unless this application creates and verifies it or tested external-tool behavior proves it. Preserve explicit overwrite warnings and make recovery behavior truthful.
- Stop dependent operations after a failed prerequisite. In particular, restore must not continue after a failed `git pull`.
- Validate configured executable, ACD, and repository paths before launching work. Distinguish process launch failure, nonzero exit, cancellation, validation failure, and dependency failure in user-visible diagnostics.
- Build process arguments with structured APIs such as `ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList` when practical; do not rely on ad hoc quoting for untrusted or user-selected paths.
- Keep the main application unelevated. Request elevation only for a narrowly scoped external action that demonstrably requires it, with explicit user consent.
- Never embed credentials, vendor media, activation data, tokens, or private download URLs. Do not bypass Studio 5000, Logix Designer SDK, Git, or Rockwell licensing and redistribution requirements.
- Verify downloaded or bundled executables using approved provenance and pinned integrity metadata before execution. Do not promise unattended installation without vendor support and clean-machine evidence.

## Validation

- Scale validation to risk. Use focused unit tests for pure logic and service behavior; add integration tests around process exit handling, cancellation, path validation, and configuration persistence when those areas change.
- For source changes, run the narrowest relevant test first, then build `src/ABLogixGitManager/ABLogixGitManager.csproj` when the environment supports the Windows WPF target.
- Do not treat a successful compile as proof of Studio 5000, Logix Designer SDK, `l5xgit`, Git credential, packaging, or clean-machine behavior. Validate those workflows in a representative Windows environment before making release claims.
- When macOS cannot execute or fully build a Windows-specific path, run all available static checks and explicitly identify the remaining Windows validation instead of implying success.
- Before finishing, inspect the focused diff for unintended changes and confirm documentation still separates current capabilities from planned ones.

## Logging Standards

Every public service method, ViewModel command, and failure path **must** write to `AppLogger`.
Failing to log is treated the same as failing to handle an error — both hide root causes.

- **Info**: Log at the start and successful end of every significant operation (config load/save, process launch, scan result, UI action that mutates state).
- **Warn**: Log every failed validation, missing file, nonzero exit code, and unexpected-but-recoverable condition.
- **Error**: Log every caught exception with the full `Exception` object (not just `.Message`). `AppLogger.Error("description", ex)` includes type, message, and stack trace.
- **Never swallow exceptions silently.** A `catch` block that does nothing is a bug. Either log and rethrow, or log and surface a message to the user.
- `AppLogger` is static, thread-safe, and never throws. It can be called from constructors, callbacks, async continuations, and background threads without guards.
- The log file path is `%APPDATA%\ABLogixGitManager\logs\app-YYYY-MM-DD.log`. Include this path in error dialogs so users can find it.
- `App.xaml.cs` registers three global exception handlers: `DispatcherUnhandledException`, `AppDomain.CurrentDomain.UnhandledException`, and `TaskScheduler.UnobservedTaskException`. These are the safety net; do not rely on them as the only log point.

- Private helpers and backing fields need comments only when the implementation is non-obvious or carries a non-obvious constraint.
- Comments explain *why*, not *what*. Do not restate the code.
- When binding `Run.Text` in XAML to a read-only (get-only) property, **always add `Mode=OneWay`**. `Run.Text` has `BindsTwoWayByDefault = true` in its DP metadata; omitting the mode causes a `XamlParseException` at startup.
- WPF-incompatible properties that look valid: `StackPanel.Spacing` (UWP/WinUI only), `TextBox.PlaceholderText` (UWP/WinUI only). Use the custom `SpacedStackPanel` control and the Grid-overlay watermark pattern respectively.
- Build process arguments with `ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList`, not `ProcessStartInfo.Arguments`. The former handles paths with spaces without manual quoting and prevents injection.

## Documentation Maintenance

- Treat the `docs/` wiki as part of the change, not a follow-up. Any commit that adds, removes, renames, or visibly changes a feature must update the matching page(s) in [docs/](/docs) in the same change, not a later one.
